venue.name: Centre of the Universe - Dominion Astrophysical Observatory
venue.description: The Centre of the Universe is the visitor centre at the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory on West Saanich Road in Victoria, a designated National Historic Site whose 1.8-metre Plaskett Telescope has been in use since June 1918. A visit combines a guided tour inside the historic Plaskett dome, a live planetarium show, and an interactive exhibit gallery with telescope models and a real meteorite. It is run by the non-profit Friends of the Dominion Astrophysical Observatory, which also runs school tours, community group tours, camp group visits and evening star parties. General admission is $21 for adults, $15 for youth aged 7 to 19 and students with valid ID, and free for kids under 6.

facility_notes.bus_parking: Parking is free at the top of the hill between the Observatory and the Visitors' Centre. There are two spaces assigned for tour buses.

restrictions: The road to the top of the hill includes a sharp hairpin bend. Please drive slowly and take care in particular with large vehicles such as coaches and motorhomes!
venue.hours_notes: Summer high season, June 16 to September 19: Tuesdays to Saturdays 11:00 AM - 6:00 PM. Winter low season, October to June 12: Fridays and Saturdays 12:00 PM - 6:00 PM. Last tour begins at 4:30 PM.
venue.seasonal_notes: Camp group visits are scheduled during the summer. Star Party Saturdays run in summer and Twilight Talks are weekly themed Friday night events.
venue.price_year_or_season: School tour cost is published as "School year 2024/5 cost: $80 per class"; general admission and group tour prices carry no date.

programs.name: School tour
programs.description: School programmes include a guided tour of the historic Plaskett Telescope, a presentation chosen from a list of grade-banded topics, a planetarium show, exploration of the gallery and other activities. Tours are 1 1/2 to 2 hours long and up to 2 classes can share a tour; transportation is arranged by schools. Slots are a 9:30am morning or a 12/12:30 afternoon start, "which can be adjusted as necessary". Topics are listed by grade band from K-1 (What's up in the sky?) to 10-12 (The Big Bang Theory).
programs.what_children_do: Go inside the dome of the 1918 Plaskett Telescope with a guide, sit for a planetarium show and a presentation on the topic the teacher picked, then move around the exhibit gallery. One grade 3-4 topic, Planets in Motion, says it will "get you up and moving too".
programs.our_note: The $80 is for the whole class, not per child, and it is still labelled 2024/5 - confirm the rate when you book. Tours only run Tuesday to Friday, and the road to the top ends in a hairpin bend a full-size bus has to take slowly.
programs.practical_summary: Parking at the top is free and two spaces are kept for tour buses. Washrooms, indoor lunch space and rain backup are not stated anywhere on the site, which is worth a call for a visit of up to two hours.

programs.name: Camp and childcare group visit
programs.description: A two-hour guided visit for day camps, recreation centres, childcare programs and community groups. Each visit includes a live planetarium show, a guided tour of the historic Observatory, an age-appropriate activity in the auditorium, time in the hands-on gallery and a themed craft to take home, all adapted to the age of the group. Programs are typically scheduled weekday mornings and afternoons during the summer, with additional times available. Groups larger than 25 may be accommodated with at least one week's advance booking.
programs.what_children_do: Sit under the planetarium dome to see stars and constellations in daylight, walk through the Observatory with a guide, do an activity in the auditorium pitched at their age, handle the gallery exhibits, and make a themed craft to take home.
programs.our_note: This is the version pitched at the youngest groups - the staff adapt it to the age of the group and it ends with something to carry out the door. You can ask for an invoice afterwards instead of paying on the day, and the booking form asks about accessibility needs, which is the place to raise them.
programs.practical_summary: Two hours, mostly indoors, with free parking and two bus spaces at the top of the hill. Washrooms, a lunch space and step-free access are not described on the site - ask when you book.
programs.payment_timing: You can pay on the day of your tour, or request an invoice to be paid afterward.

programs.name: Community group tour
programs.description: A guided tour for Girl Guides, Scouts, youth clubs and other community groups. It includes a guided tour of the historic Observatory, a planetarium presentation of stars, planets and constellations, and time to explore hands-on gallery exhibits. Cost is $10.00 per participant with leaders included, for groups of up to 20; larger groups may be accommodated with advance notice. Tours are typically offered evenings and weekends, with flexible scheduling.
programs.what_children_do: Follow a guide through the Observatory, sit for a planetarium presentation of the stars, planets and constellations, then spend time at the hands-on exhibits in the gallery.
programs.our_note: This one runs evenings and weekends rather than in the school day, so it suits after-school clubs and Guide units more than a daycare morning. The $10 covers leaders as well as children, which is worth knowing when you count heads.
programs.practical_summary: Free parking with two bus spaces at the top of a steep road with a hairpin bend. Nothing is published about washrooms, lunch space or step-free access, so ask in the booking email.
